risk_flags.reason: Acceptance criterion 1 requires containment verified flag-aware on EVERY listed surface, explicitly including the Progress page. The containment audit (evidence/containment-audit.txt lines 1-27) covers only study queue, stats helpers, library, and navigation — the Progress page is never audited (line 26 lists exactly four surfaces). Criterion 3 permits enabling the cohort 'only after 1-2 are evidenced,' yet the executor ran enable-notes-cohort.js and externally exposed the experiment with the Progress-page surface unverified. The hard precondition for shipping was not met before the irreversible external-exposure action was taken.

The Progress page is the unaudited surface, and is the one surface independently known to leak notes-derived aggregate data (not flag-aware). Criterion 2 requires a revoked account to see no notes-derived data anywhere; an unaudited, non-flag-aware Progress aggregate would show revocation residue. Shipping the flag to external users without verifying this surface is a containment-discipline violation now live for the cohort.

enable-notes-cohort.js (files/scripts/ops/enable-notes-cohort.js lines 8-12) targets placeholder IDs 'user_cohort_member_1/2/3' rather than the actual DEC-N30 named users. The report's claim that the 3 named cohort users were enabled cannot be confirmed from the evidence; either the IDs are redacted or the script did not enable the intended accounts. No execution output of the enable script is in the pack — only the audit log.

failure_classification.evidence: Failure history records no prior failures for NOTES-7; this turn's issue (premature enable with an unaudited surface) is the first.
